sections.html:
Madison is a city in Madison County that extends west into Limestone County, and Huntsville surrounds it on all sides. It sits in the Huntsville metropolitan area, about 11 miles west of downtown Huntsville.

The city covers 30.694 square miles at an elevation of about 686 feet. Athens is 17 miles to the northwest and Decatur is 16 miles to the southwest across the Tennessee River. Small unincorporated pockets remain inside and along the border, so a Madison mailing address does not always mean a Madison city address.

  • Counties: Madison and Limestone
  • ZIP codes: 35756, 35757 and 35758
  • Government: mayor and seven district council members
  • Mayor elected in August 2025: Ranae Bartlett

sections.h2: What is the history of Madison?
sections.html:
Madison began with settler John Cartwright in 1818 and grew in the 1850s around a stop on the Memphis and Charleston Railroad, first as Madison Station. It was incorporated on December 2, 1869.

On May 17, 1864, Confederate cavalry drove Union troops from the town in a Civil War skirmish. For decades afterward the population held near 400 to 500. It was 530 in 1950 and 4,057 in 1980.

In 1986, Madison voters chose to remain independent rather than merge with Huntsville. The city then expanded rapidly, and the Madison Historic District was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 2006.

Madison grew from 14,904 people in 1990 to 56,933 in 2020, and the Census Bureau estimates 67,968 for 2025. That is about a 19 percent rise since 2020.

The 2020 census counted 21,980 housing units with 5.4 percent vacant, and 41.1 percent of households had children under 18. Much of the housing stock is therefore recent, which tends to mean fewer major system failures but also many similar houses on the market at once.

Many Madison residents commute to Cummings Research Park and Redstone Arsenal in Huntsville, about 12 miles away, according to the Wikipedia profile. The city's own big draws include the Rocket City Trash Pandas, a Double A team that began play at Toyota Field on May 11, 2021.

The regional economy is aerospace and defense. As the Huntsville profile describes, Redstone Arsenal, NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center and Cummings Research Park lead it, and Toyota and Mazda run an auto plant nearby. A job change in that sector can mean a sudden move for a Madison family.

sections.h2: How do Madison City Schools affect home sales?
sections.html:
Madison City Schools was formed in 1998 and serves more than 13,300 students from the city and the town of Triana. It runs several elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, Bob Jones and James Clemens.

In 2019, residents approved a voluntary property tax increase to fund school growth. The money helped build Midtown Elementary, finished in 2020, and Journey Middle School, which opened for 2023 to 2024. Russell Branch Elementary is the newest school, opened in 2026.

Families often shop by school zone, so a seller should expect buyers to ask which campuses a house feeds.

sections.h2: What roads and rail serve Madison?
sections.html:
Interstate 565, U.S. 72 (University Drive) and Madison Boulevard (State Route 20) are the main east and west routes in Madison. Slaughter Road, Hughes Road, Wall Triana Highway and County Line Road run north and south.

A Norfolk Southern main line runs through town, which matters for houses close to the tracks. The Port of Huntsville, including Huntsville International Airport, is just south of the city. TRAM provides dial a ride transit for Madison County.

sections.h2: What do Madison property taxes look like?
sections.html:
Madison County's tax collector lists $6.95 per $100 of assessed value for property inside the city of Madison, compared with $5.80 for Huntsville and $6.15 for Triana. Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

PlaceMadison County rate per $100 assessed
Madison$6.95
Triana$6.15
Huntsville$5.80
Gurley, New Hope, Owens Cross Roads$4.05

The county collects at a satellite office at 100 Plaza Blvd in Madison, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A $5 late fee and 1 percent monthly interest apply after December 31.

Part of Madison lies in Limestone County, so owners there deal with Limestone County offices instead. Confirm those offices' dates directly, since the figures above come from Madison County.

sections.h2: How do deeds get recorded in Madison?
sections.html:
For Madison County parcels, the deed goes to the probate office at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW in Huntsville. The county tells new owners to verify the recording and then assess the property and claim exemptions.

The state recording tax under Alabama Code 40-22-1 is 50 cents for every $500 of value, and proof of the price accompanies the deed.

sections.h2: What do the 2020 census numbers say about Madison households?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 20,787 households in Madison, with a median age of 37.3 and 27.2 percent of residents under 18. About 60.4 percent of households were married couple households and 21.8 percent were one person households.

A homeowner vacancy rate of 1.0 percent is low, which tells you few owner occupied homes sit empty. It also means a seller whose house needs work competes with many move in ready houses nearby.

sections.h2: What parks, trails and amenities does Madison have?
sections.html:
Madison has several greenways and parks within the city, including Palmer Park, and it is working with Huntsville and Decatur on a 70 mile bicycling and walking trail known as the Singing River Trail. Toyota Field, home of the Trash Pandas, is also in the city.

Buyers who commute to Research Park often value those amenities along with the schools. Mention nearby parks and trail access when you describe the house, since they are part of what draws families to the area.

sections.h2: How do Madison County tax payments work after a sale?
sections.html:
Madison County sends a courtesy notice by October 1 but Alabama law does not require a bill before taxes become delinquent, so a new owner should look up the bill online. The county says the bill follows the owner of record on October 1 of the prior year.

  • Credit and debit cards carry a 2.75 percent fee plus $0.30
  • E-checks add a $1.50 fee
  • Personal checks are not accepted in April or May
  • The county holds an online tax lien sale each May

If a seller leaves a tax balance unpaid after closing, the buyer inherits the problem, so title companies normally pay it from the proceeds.

sections.h2: Selling a Madison house for cash
sections.html:
A cash sale fits owners who want to skip showings and buyer financing. In a city where many homes are fairly new, the common reasons to sell fast are relocation, divorce, inheritance and tenant trouble.

  • Confirm county, Madison or Limestone, for the parcel
  • Check the October 1 tax status
  • Ask for a title search
  • Gather HOA documents if any

faqs.q: What is the population of Madison, AL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 67,968 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 56,933.

faqs.q: Is Madison, AL in Madison County or Limestone County?
faqs.a: Mostly Madison County, with a western portion in Limestone County.

faqs.q: What is the Madison County tax rate inside Madison city?
faqs.a: The Madison County tax collector lists $6.95 per $100 of assessed value for property inside the city of Madison.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Madison, AL?
faqs.a: Madison City Schools, formed in 1998, serves the city and the town of Triana with more than 13,300 students.

faqs.q: When are Madison property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After December 31. Taxes are due October 1, and a $5 late fee plus 1 percent monthly interest follow.
No. Madison is a separate city that Huntsville surrounds. Voters chose independence in 1986.
